reference_use.conclusion: Snapshot project d09bc8a / Mathlib 25730c7c plus the pinned simongmt package. No match: Mathlib has no co-area formula (rg 'coarea': no file) and only a fixed-dimension Sard lemma (MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean), no C¹ Sard-type slice theorem and no countable rectifiability; SimonGMT has no nonlinear co-area formula. Hence the C¹ critical-slice estimate, the C¹ parametric co-area formula and the level-set rectifiability are supplied as children. Available and cited in the children: SimonGMT linear/projection co-area (CoareaLinear.lean, CoareaProjection.lean), Lipschitz and injective area formulas (AreaDomain.lean weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn, ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension, exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional; WeightedArea.lean map_withDensity_areaJacobian_eq and weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative for arbitrary integrands), Lipschitz image bound euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, countablyRectifiable_image_contDiffOn_open / _iUnion / _of_measure_zero / CountablyRectifiable.mono, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (needs only θ x ≠ 0); Mathlib normDet (normDet_comp, normDet_of_subsingleton, normDet_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot, normDet_sq), μHE[d] = c_d·μH[d] with hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_sum, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, inverse/implicit function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm, HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorph), change of variables lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul, Lusin-Souslin MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn / ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding, lintegral_iUnion (arbitrary integrand), lintegral_tsum, lintegral_liminf_le, HasLineDerivAt.unique, Rademacher LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp. subproblem.title: Countably many C¹ chart pieces on which f agrees to first order with C¹ maps (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, Remark 1.3 and Ch. 2, Thm 1.5)
subproblem.statement: Assume Lemma 1.2 in the frozen form SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization and the C¹ approximation theorem in exactly the frozen form of the root-level sibling lipschitz_c1_approximation: (C1) for all n, p, every K-Lipschitz F : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ and every ε > 0 there is g : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ of class C¹ with Lⁿ({x : F(x) ≠ g(x) or DF(x) ≠ Dg(x)}) < ε. Let n, ℓ, m ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} countably n-rectifiable, U ⊇ M open and f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → ℝᵐ locally Lipschitz on U. Then there are sequences (j ∈ ℕ) D_j ⊆ ℝⁿ, ψ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ}, G_j : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ and E_j ⊆ ℝⁿ such that: D_j is open; ψ_j is C¹ on D_j, injective on D_j and Lipschitz on D_j, with Dψ_j(u) injective for every u ∈ D_j; G_j is C¹ on ℝⁿ; E_j is Borel and E_j ⊆ D_j; for every u ∈ E_j, f(ψ_j(u)) = G_j(u) and f ∘ ψ_j has Fréchet derivative DG_j(u) at u; and Hⁿ(M \ ⋃_j ψ_j(E_j)) = 0. Notation (as in the parent): ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hˢ = μHE[s] (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Hausdorff outer measure); Lᵈ = volume; normDet = Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet; P* = LinearMap.adjoint P; DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u.
subproblem.lean_statement: SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization → (∀ (n p : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn p) (K : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith K f → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ g : Rn n → Rn p, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ volume {x | f x ≠ g x ∨ fderiv ℝ f x ≠ fderiv ℝ g x} < ε) → ∀ (n ℓ m : ℕ) (M U : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))) (f : Rn (n + ℓ) → Rn m), CountablyRectifiable n M → IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ∃ (D : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (ψ : ℕ → Rn n → Rn (n + ℓ)) (G : ℕ → Rn n → Rn m) (E : ℕ → Set (Rn n)), (∀ j, IsOpen (D j)) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (ψ j) (D j)) ∧ (∀ j, InjOn (ψ j) (D j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ K, LipschitzOnWith K (ψ j) (D j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∀ u ∈ D j, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ (ψ j) u)) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G j)) ∧ (∀ j, MeasurableSet (E j)) ∧ (∀ j, E j ⊆ D j) ∧ (∀ j, ∀ u ∈ E j, f (ψ j u) = G j u ∧ HasFDerivAt (f ∘ ψ j) (fderiv ℝ (G j) u) u) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ j, ψ j '' E j) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Parts 1.1, 1.3 and 2.1 (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and Remark 1.3, chapter-03.txt lines 25-73, and the procedure of the area formula, lines 376-381, invoked for the co-area formula at lines 426-428 and for the slices at lines 440-442; C¹ Approximation Theorem 1.5 and Rademacher's Theorem 1.4 of Ch. 2). Departures from the parent's 1.1/1.3, stated explicitly: ψ_α is only required to be Lipschitz (not bi-Lipschitz) on D_α, which is all the later steps use; the agreement of derivatives is recorded as the Fréchet derivative of f∘ψ_α at u (the parent's Dh_α(u) = DG(u)); and E_{α,i} does not remove the exceptional set Z_α of the chart lemma, which is instead handled where it is used (siblings chart_piece_coarea_formula and coarea_tangent_existence). No measurability of M is needed here.
1. (Submanifold cover.) By the forward direction of SubmanifoldCoverCharacterization (for n, ℓ, M), M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_{i∈ℕ} N_i with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 and each N_i satisfying IsC1Submanifold n: every y ∈ N_i has V ⊆ ℝⁿ, W ∋ y open and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+ℓ} with ψ C¹ and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N_i and Dψ(x) injective for x ∈ V.
2. (Countably many submanifold charts.) Fix i. The open sets W (one chosen for each y ∈ N_i) cover N_i; ℝ^{n+ℓ} is second countable, so countably many of them, with charts (V_{i,r}, ψ_{i,r}), r ∈ ℕ, cover N_i (Lindelöf).
3. (Good balls inside one chart.) Fix a chart (V, ψ) from step 2 and put V' := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U), open since ψ is continuous on the open V and U is open. For u ∈ V', x := ψ(u) ∈ U; local Lipschitz continuity of f on the open U gives s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ U and f Lipschitz on B_s(x). By continuity of ψ at u choose r_u > 0 with closedBall(u, r_u) ⊆ V' and ψ(closedBall(u, r_u)) ⊆ B_s(x). Dψ is continuous on V (ψ is C¹ on the open V), hence bounded on the compact convex closedBall(u, r_u) ⊆ V, so ψ is Lipschitz on it by the mean value inequality (Mathlib ContDiffOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith / Convex.lipschitzOnWith_of_nnnorm_fderivWithin_le); put D := B_{r_u}(u). Then ψ is C¹, injective and Lipschitz on D with injective derivative, and h := f ∘ ψ is Lipschitz on D (composition, ψ(D) ⊆ B_s(x)). By Lindelöf, countably many of the balls B_{r_u}(u), u ∈ V', cover V'.
4. (Enumeration and coverage.) Collecting the balls of step 3 over all charts of step 2 and all i (and padding with empty charts D = ∅, ψ = 0 if necessary) gives (D_α, ψ_α), α ∈ ℕ, with the chart properties of the statement and h_α := f ∘ ψ_α Lipschitz on D_α. If x ∈ M \ N₀, then x ∈ N_i for some i, x ∈ W_{i,r} ∩ N_i = ψ_{i,r}(V_{i,r}) for some r, so x = ψ_{i,r}(u) with u ∈ V_{i,r}, and u ∈ V'_{i,r} because x ∈ M ⊆ U; hence u lies in one of the chosen balls. Thus M \ N₀ ⊆ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α).
5. (C¹ approximation; parent 1.3.) Fix α. Extend h_α|_{D_α} to a Lipschitz map h̃_α : ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ (coordinatewise McShane extension, Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; SimonGMT exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional). For i ≥ 1, (C1) with ε = 1/i gives G_{α,i} of class C¹ with Lⁿ(Bad_{α,i}) < 1/i, Bad_{α,i} := {h̃_α ≠ G_{α,i}} ∪ {Dh̃_α ≠ DG_{α,i}}. Put E_{α,i} := D_α ∩ Diff(h̃_α) ∩ {h̃_α = G_{α,i}} ∩ {Dh̃_α = DG_{α,i}}, Diff(h̃_α) the set of differentiability points of h̃_α. E_{α,i} is Borel: Diff(h̃_α) is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), {h̃_α = G_{α,i}} is closed, and {Dh̃_α = DG_{α,i}} is Borel because u ↦ Dh̃_α(u) and u ↦ DG_{α,i}(u) are Borel maps (measurable_fderiv) into the finite-dimensional, hence second-countable, space of continuous linear maps, whose diagonal is measurable (measurableSet_eq_fun).
6. (Agreement to first order.) Let u ∈ E_{α,i}. Then f(ψ_α(u)) = h_α(u) = h̃_α(u) = G_{α,i}(u). Since D_α is open and h̃_α = f ∘ ψ_α on D_α, the two maps coincide on a neighbourhood of u; h̃_α is differentiable at u with Dh̃_α(u) = DG_{α,i}(u); hence f ∘ ψ_α has Fréchet derivative DG_{α,i}(u) at u.
7. (Full measure in each chart.) D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i} ⊆ (ℝⁿ \ Diff(h̃_α)) ∪ ⋂_i Bad_{α,i}. The first set is Lⁿ-null by Rademacher's theorem (h̃_α is Lipschitz; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), and Lⁿ(⋂_i Bad_{α,i}) ≤ inf_i 1/i = 0. So Lⁿ(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}) = 0.
8. (Null images.) ψ_α is Lipschitz on D_α, so Hⁿ(ψ_α(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i})) ≤ Lip(ψ_α)ⁿ·Hⁿ(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}) = Lip(ψ_α)ⁿ·Lⁿ(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}) = 0 (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn; Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
9. (Conclusion.) Re-index the pairs (α, i) by j ∈ ℕ through a bijection ℕ × ℕ ≅ ℕ and set D_j := D_α, ψ_j := ψ_α, G_j := G_{α,i}, E_j := E_{α,i}; steps 3-6 give all the listed properties. If x ∈ M \ N₀ then x = ψ_α(u) with u ∈ D_α (step 4); either u ∈ E_{α,i} for some i, so x ∈ ⋃_j ψ_j(E_j), or u ∈ D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}. Hence M \ ⋃_j ψ_j(E_j) ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_α ψ_α(D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i}), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets (steps 1, 8). ∎
proof_key_steps: Lemma 1.2 gives M ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ N_i with C¹ submanifolds N_i; Lindelöf gives countably many submanifold charts.

Inside each chart choose countably many small balls D_α (closure in the chart, image inside U where f is Lipschitz): ψ_α is C¹, injective, Lipschitz with injective derivative and f∘ψ_α is Lipschitz; M \ N₀ ⊆ ⋃ ψ_α(D_α).
Lipschitz extension of f∘ψ_α and C¹ approximation (C1) with ε = 1/i; Borel agreement sets E_{α,i} where values and derivatives agree.
Rademacher: D_α \ ⋃_i E_{α,i} is Lⁿ-null, so its ψ_α-image is Hⁿ-null.

audit.reason: All chart and agreement properties in the Lean conclusion are constructed. Small chart balls ensure Lipschitz bounds; extension, C¹ approximation and Rademacher give Borel first-order agreement sets with null complement. Lipschitz image bounds prove the required coverage without assuming M measurable.
